trial_court: Special Court of Judicial First Class Magistrate (NI Act Cases), Kozhikode - Crl.A No.89 of 2017
case_name: Kalathil Hamsakoya vs Rajashekar Palakkavu Kalam And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: Rajashekar Palakkavu Kalam, aged 56 years (complainant) & State of Kerala

facts_of_case: Complaint alleging cheque bounce; accused pleaded not guilty and faced trial; trial court found him guilty and sentenced to pay a fine.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to explain how his signed cheque reached the hands of the complainant.
legal_principles.held: Accordingly, the accused has no explanation as to how his signed cheque reached at the hands of the complainant.

legal_principles.principle: A cheque is dishonoured if it is returned due to insufficient funds in the account of the accused.
legal_principles.held: Ext.P4 memo would show that Ext.P3 cheque was dishonoured due to insufficient funds in the account of the accused.

outcome.final_order: Concurrent verdict of conviction and order of sentence against the revision petitioner by the trial court and appellate court for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

use_for_drafting: drafting a cheque bounce case in the High Court of Kerala
preparing a criminal revision petition under Section 397 CrPC
responding to a demand notice for payment
